clue.text: Profitable source of energy promoted in America, oil perhaps

indicators.note: promoted means moved up to an earlier place, so the letter is shifted towards the front of the across entry

parts.note: oil is one example of a fuel

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Oil is touted in America as a lucrative source of power.
explanation.walkthrough: Write US then FUEL (USFUEL); 'promoted' moves the E (from 'source of energy') two places forward to give USEFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something profitable is of benefit or advantage, which is what useful means.

clue.text: Sound sleepers make love, getting up around noon

indicators.note: around tells us one piece wraps round the other, here the upturned word goes round the single letter
getting up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: Lovers rise to make love around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns EROS into SORE, and 'around' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A snore is the noise that heavy sleepers produce, so the definition is a little descriptive phrase for it.

clue.text: Cool orangeade's temperature is almost cold

parts.note: Fanta is a brand of orangeade; with the possessive S it gives FANTAS

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: icy means very cold

explanation.surface: A chilled orange drink is described as being nearly cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ICY to IC; 'is' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool as slang for excellent is a near-synonym of fantastic.

clue.text: Taste defeat

definitions.meaning: to taste it with the tongue
... is informal for beat or defeat, as in 'we ... them'

explanation.surface: Two words that read like getting a bitter experience of losing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lick is both a tongue action used for tasting and slang for thrashing an opponent.

clue.text: Peter out to relax after month with runs

indicators.note: after signals that the word for relax comes behind the month and the runs

parts.note: Dec is short for December
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to ease is to relax

explanation.surface: Peter is told to go out and relax after a month of scoring runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name but 'Peter out' is the verb phrase defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to diminish gradually, a synonym of decrease.

clue.text: That's highly unlikely, say Watson and Holmes shortly

parts.note: Holmes's companion is Dr Watson, giving DR

indicators.note: shortly means the name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Eamonn Holmes is a British TV presenter

explanation.surface: Watson and Holmes declare something very improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants Sherlock Holmes, but this Holmes is Eamonn Holmes, a British breakfast-TV presenter; 'shortly' drops a final N.
explanation.definitionFit: Dream on is a sarcastic retort meaning what you hope for will never happen.

clue.text: Miss amusing dinner invitation hosts sent without envelope

indicators.note: hosts means holding something inside, so the dinner invitation contains the other piece

parts.note: 'Come dine' is an invitation to dinner

indicators.note: taking away the envelope removes the outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A young woman is amused by a dinner invitation sent without an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without envelope' strips SENT to EN, and 'hosts' puts it inside COME DINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedienne is a female comic: a woman whose job is to entertain and make people laugh.

clue.text: Giant metal vessel carries creature from outer space

indicators.note: in a down clue, carries means the vessel holds the creature up on top of it

parts.note: ET is the alien from the film E.T.
a tin is a metal container

explanation.surface: A huge metal ship carries an alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' in a down clue puts ET above TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ettin is a two-headed giant in English folklore and fantasy games.

clue.text: Filbert's leaving Burma entering Chinese republic

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Sino- is a prefix meaning Chinese

indicators.note: leaving means these letters depart from the country's name

parts.note: Myanmar is the current name of Burma
the setter is Filbert, so Filbert's means my

explanation.surface: The setter departs Burma to go into China.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Filbert's' simply means 'my'; Burma's modern name supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: My special place way down the coast

parts.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like My!
a niche is a place suited to someone

explanation.surface: Someone describes their favourite spot somewhere along the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation here, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coastline.

clue.text: Medium uniform given to very short rebel

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
tiny means very small

explanation.surface: A medium-sized uniform is issued to a tiny rebel soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutiny is to revolt against authority, especially aboard ship or in the army.

clue.text: Star Victor Mature making a comeback

parts.note: V is victor in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: making a comeback means the word comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: to mature is to age

explanation.surface: Film star Victor Mature returns to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor Mature was a Hollywood actor, but here his names are split: V plus AGE reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is one of the brightest stars in the night sky, in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Mary delirious about new introduction to Adonis

parts.note: mad can mean wildly excited or delirious
on means about, as in a talk on a topic

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Mary is beside herself about meeting a new Adonis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madonna is a title of the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: On vacation Susan has trouble with room rate that's poor

indicators.note: on vacation means the word is vacated, emptied of its inner letters

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
room means space

explanation.surface: Susan is on holiday and complains about her room and its poor rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' empties Susan to SN; 'has' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail's pace is a very slow speed, so a poor rate of progress.

clue.text: Innocent frolics before church, no sex

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged word ahead of the church
frolics suggests playful jumping about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Innocent fun before church, with nothing sexual involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolics' rearranges INNOCENT into CONTINEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Continence is self-restraint, especially abstaining from sexual activity.

clue.text: Design a long coat shaped like an umbrella?

indicators.note: design means arrange or plan, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion designer plans a long raincoat cut like an umbrella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design' rearranges A LONG COAT; the question mark flags that an umbrella is only one eight-sided example.
explanation.definitionFit: A typical umbrella has eight ribs, so its canopy seen from above is eight-sided.

clue.text: Cut material for the floor, moving in later

indicators.note: moving, paired with later, shifts a pair of letters to a further position in the word
later says where the moved letters end up: further along the word

parts.note: lino is a floor covering

explanation.surface: Cutting flooring material and then moving in afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving in later' shifts the IN of LINO along by one, giving LOIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A loin is a cut of meat from an animal's back.

clue.text: Disturbance in Molière, Act I gone?

definitions.text: Disturbance in Molière, Act I gone?

indicators.note: disturbance means the letters in these words are thrown into disorder
gone says this letter disappears from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone disrupts a Molière play, having missed the first act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes I from MOLIERE ACT, then 'Disturbance in' rearranges the rest. Read whole, the clue describes the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A latecomer arriving after the first act would disturb the audience at a play.

clue.text: Touching your ears is old idiosyncrasy

parts.note: a tic is a habitual quirk

explanation.surface: Fiddling with your ears is a longstanding quirk.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is an anatomical adjective meaning relating to the ear.

clue.text: Popular meeting place, usually a bar

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a junction is where roads or lines meet

explanation.surface: A popular rendezvous is generally a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means a ban; 'usually a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An injunction is a court order prohibiting something, so a legal bar.

clue.text: Only cool person on the bench

parts.note: just means only
to ice is to cool

explanation.surface: The only cool person sitting on the substitutes' bench.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice is a judge, who sits on the judicial bench.

clue.text: European intelligence agency goes after information source

indicators.note: goes after places the European agency behind the information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
SIS is the Secret Intelligence Service, Britain's MI6

explanation.surface: A European spy agency pursues the source of some intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means origin or beginning, the source from which something comes.

clue.text: Presumably all disagreeing in corners

definitions.meaning: if everyone disagrees there are ..., read as ...

explanation.surface: Everyone in the corners seems to be arguing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as NO OKS: nobody saying OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks are secluded corners or recesses in a room.

clue.text: Fifth baby, wanting eight perhaps

indicators.note: wanting here means coming short of, so the letter is placed after the baby to complete it

parts.note: a cub is a young animal
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A fifth child is born, while the parents had hoped for eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is two multiplied by itself three times, so it is a perfect cube number.

clue.text: Too many bottles in dustbin, generally

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: There are generally too many empty bottles in the rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of excessive drinking, getting through too many bottles.

clue.text: Excitedly close high value contract

definitions.meaning: to shut something forcefully, as a door in anger
in bridge a ... is a contract to win all or all but one trick

explanation.surface: Eagerly closing a lucrative business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slamming is shutting with force, and a slam is the top bid in the card game bridge.

clue.text: Fur shared by a couple of orangutangs

indicators.note: shared by tells us the answer is held within the doubled word, straddling the join, so the surrounding letters are discarded
a couple of means two copies of the word are written side by side

explanation.surface: Two orangutans have the same fur.
explanation.walkthrough: Write ORANGUTANGS twice: the answer runs across the join, from the end of the first into the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is the soft hair of the Angora rabbit or goat, used as a fur or wool.

clue.text: Brighten up run-down university, the one I went to

parts.note: run-down means unwell, ill
the one belonging to me is mine

explanation.surface: Someone wants to smarten up their shabby old university.
explanation.definitionFit: Illumine is a literary word for light up, to make bright.

clue.text: Prosthetic leg's easy to replace

indicators.note: to replace means the letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: An artificial leg is simple to swap in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace' rearranges LEGS EASY; the S of leg's is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass eye is an artificial eye, a prosthetic replacing a lost one.

clue.text: A bit of food left by solver who preferred a pint

parts.note: Inspector Morse, the TV detective, solved crimes and loved a pint of beer

explanation.surface: A scrap of food is left behind by a beer-drinking crossword solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a British TV detective famous for real ale and crosswords; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small piece or mouthful of food.
